prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "Apply computer vision expertise to this task". The fixture contains version/runtime ambiguity, a tempting shortcut, a compatibility edge case, and a failure path that distinguishes real expertise from generic completion. The acceptance boundary is computer-vision: Define task, labels, camera/image formation, resolution, geometry, lighting, occlusion, populations, deployment hardware, and acceptable error tradeoffs. The adjacent fine-tuning-training discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

requirements: production-lot/camera/time grouped images with polygon/raster masks, uncertain regions and duplicate crops
baseline/candidate preprocessing and geometric augmentation implementations
pinned segmentation model/weights/class map plus mask/decision threshold candidates and prediction fixtures
per-class/tiny-defect/lighting/material/device metrics plus exported-runtime and accelerator traces
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual computer-vision boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=implementation; near-neighbor=fine-tuning-training), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Define task, labels, camera/image formation, resolution, geometry, lighting, occlusion, populations, deployment hardware, and acceptable error tradeoffs.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.
Evaluate held-out slices across lighting, scale, occlusion, background, device, demographic or environmental factors where relevant, plus latency/memory on target hardware and confidence calibration.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not let random image splits leak near-duplicates, use augmentation that changes labels, generalize studio benchmarks to field conditions, or hide systematic slice failures in aggregate accuracy.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Camera/image-formation, label ontology, spatial geometry and transform identity; Leakage-safe grouped splits plus task-correct vision metrics and deployment slices; Model/preprocess/postprocess/calibration identity with visual or machine-readable failure evidence; Target-runtime latency/memory/throughput plus reproducible promotion and rollback artifacts), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
